title: R' Abba bar Hamnuna
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Hyman cites him only in the Jerusalem Talmud, at the end of Gittin 8:3: Rabbi Yaakov bar Acha, Rabbi Ba bar Hamnuna, in the name of Rav Ada bar Achvah (Ahavah), concerning Shabbat. There, in 9:3: Rabbi Ba bar Hamnuna, Rav Ada bar Acha (Ahavah), in the name of Rav, that it is Rabbi Meir’s view.

notes.text: The two compressed chains do not explicitly supply every reporting link. Achvah/Acha and the parenthetical Ahavah proposals are retained separately.

The two saved whole Mechon-Mamre Gittin8:3 and9:3 scalars attest Yaakov bar Acha, Ba bar Hamnuna, Ada bar Achvah/Acha and the Rav/Meir reporting formula. The8:3 scalar explicitly spells full Rabbi for Yaakov and Ba;9:3 explicitly spells Rabbi Meir. This supports these exact connected occurrences without adding every intermediate reporting connector. Heading Abba remains distinct from body Ba; its abbreviated title stays R'. Supplied Ahavah parenthetical alternatives remain Hyman’s proposals, not adopted personal names or identities. סה״ג means end of halakhah3, not merely section3.

The printed Hebrew preserves Ba in the two quotations and Abba in the heading. The Mechon Mamre and Guggenheimer Hebrew witnesses retain Rav Ada bar Achvah in 8:3 and Rav Ada bar Acha in 9:3. In his note to 9:3, Guggenheimer proposes reading a sequence of Rabbi Acha, Rav Hamnuna, and Rav Ada bar Achvah instead. That proposal and Hyman’s parenthetical Ahavah are separate conjectures. The Hebrew passages leave some reporting links unstated.
